citations.narrative:
In the walk-through area of the park, the enclosures housing emus had numerous sharp points that may cause injury to
the animals.
-The enclosure near the back area of the exhibit housing two emus had broken pieces of wire with sharp points extending
into the enclosure. The sharp points were at eye level height. Two nails were extending upward from a railroad tie on the
ground next to the shelter.
-The enclosure near the front of the exhibit housing two emus had a loose board with two screws that were extending into
the enclosure. The sharp points were approximately 12 inches above the ground.
Housing facilities for birds must be designed and constructed so that they are structurally sound for the species of bird
housed in them. They must be kept in good repair and protect the birds from injury.
Corrected at time of inspection.

- The herd of adult Jacob's sheep have heavy wool coats and are overdue for shearing. The wool burden on these sheep
puts them at risk of heat stress as the summer temperatures increase. These animals need to be properly sheared well
before the arrival of high summer temperatures. The facility needs to have these animals sheared as soon as possible to
protect against the climactic conditions present in this part of the country.
Correct by: 30 June 2026

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
The enclosure for the ringtail lemur had numerous flying insects on and around the food receptacle and covering the food
itself. When the licensee touched the food container, a mass of insects flew up. Insects are a potential source of
contamination to the feed and could potentially cause irritation or injury to the animal itself. Food contaminated by pests
may harbor disease causing organisms that could affect the health of the animal. The pest control program used by the
facility was not effective in controlling the pests.
An effective program for control of insects, external parasites affecting nonhuman primates, and birds and mammals that
are pests, must be established and maintained so as to promote the health and well- being of the animals and reduce
contamination by pests in animal areas.
To be corrected by 6-18-2026.

Several areas of the facility needed repair and maintenance. All structures must be maintained in good repair to help
protect the enclosed animals.
-The enclosure for a young lamb had loose wires with sharp points on a sheet of wire covering the door. The sharp points
were at eye level height of the lamb and protruded into the enclosure.
The outdoor enclosure for three Jacob sheep and a Pere David’s deer had several pieces of wire around the enclosure
that had sharp points extending into the enclosure. The sharp points were at eye level to the animals. There were pieces
of scrap metal with sharp edges lying on the ground in the enclosure.
The outdoor enclosure for a coatimundi had a piece of wire with a sharp point extending from the climbing branch. The
inside of the enclosure had numerous areas with loose wires with sharp points around the inside wall of the enclosure.
Sharp points and edges are a potential source of injury to enclosed animals. The indoor and outdoor housing facilities
shall be structurally sound and shall be maintained in good repair to protect the animals from injury and to contain the
animals.
Corrected at time of inspection.

- The kinkajou in the reception area was being fed small quantities of m&m candy as a treat. Chocolate is potentially toxic
to kinkajous and is not an appropriate part of the diet. All feed must be appropriate for the species of animal, taking into
consideration their age and health.
Facility removed the candy at the time of inspection and stated that it would no longer be fed to the kinkajou.
Corrected at time of inspection
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative.
Additional Inspectors:
Michael Tygart, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
